inspection_outcome: Four established issues: one Major construction failure and three bounded Minor statements; exact version attribution
summary: Explicit product-of-norms comparison fails finite étale base change; H4 vanishing boundary, missing Postnikov action and disconnected global End1 also corrected. No principal-classification counterexample.
limitations: Primary is arXiv v2, not verified publisher-equivalent
Later author PDF only locally collated
General repair of comparison morphism and all higher coherences not certified

problems.title: Separate norms fail base-change naturality
problems.claim: The product of individual coordinate norms defines a presheaf morphism Z_tr(G_m^n) -> K_n.
problems.assumptions: F=Q perfect, Y=Spec Q[s±1,t±1], Z=Spec Q[u±1,t±1], s=u². Z embeds by x²=s,y=t and is integral finite étale degree 2 over smooth Y.
problems.check_method: Exact finite étale splitting and Quillen K2 tame symbol
problems.decisive_evidence: The rule before base change is {-s,t²}; after pullback to Z it is 2{-u²,t}. The pulled-back correspondence is the sum of the multiplicity-one graphs (u,t),(-u,t), so additivity of the rule gives {-u²,t}. Difference {-u²,t} has nontrivial t-adic tame boundary -u² in Q(u)*.
problems.result: Fails naturality even for an ordinary presheaf; generic nonzero difference survives Zariski sheafification.
problems.counterevidence: A standard motivic-K2 comparison may still exist; no counterexample to the principal classification. Later author PDF p19 retains same formula.
problems.impact: The explicit (2.16) and specified comparison (2.19), Theorem 2.3.8 and use in 2.3.11 lack the claimed construction.

correction.statement: Use transfer of the product, not product of transfers; in this example Tr{u,t}={-s,t}.
correction.verification: Exact local projection-formula repair and split base change verified. General map on finite correspondences and full descent/compatibilities not proved here.
correction.status: local repair only; general replacement construction unverified
correction.author_adoption: No communication; formula remains in separately viewed later author manuscript.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Section2.3.5, Eq2.16 and the proposed transfer-compatible map Eq2.19 on author-v2 p20 use the separate norms of two units on an integral finite correspondence. Theorem2.3.8 and Proposition2.3.11 use this comparison.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: Primary checked the exact formula and the finite ?tale example Y=Spec Q[s?1,t?1], Z=Spec Q[u?1,t?1], s=u?. The correspondence x?=s,y=t has separate-norm symbol {-s,t?}; its pullback is 2{-u?,t}. The split graphs after this base change instead sum to {u,t}+{-u,t}={-u?,t}. Their difference has tame boundary -u? at t=0 in Q(u)(t), which is nontrivial. Thus the failure survives the generic Milnor-K2 and sheaf comparison; it is not merely a presentation discrepancy.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: A genuine transfer Tr{u,t} gives {-s,t} in this example, but that calculation alone does not construct the claimed general map. The defect breaks the stated weight-two comparison and its subsequent square, while no counterexample to the principal metaplectic classification is established. The separately inspected later author text still prints the same separate-norm formula.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: Replace the separate norm construction by a rigorously transfer-compatible map and re-prove the comparison and compatibility square; a local formula substitution is not certified as a complete repair.

problems.title: Global motivic H4 is not zero
problems.claim: For connected smooth X/F, H^i_Zar(X,Z(2))=0 for i>=4, attributed to Kahn Theorem 1.6.
problems.assumptions: F=Q, X=P²_Q smooth connected; section convention is global derived cohomology, not cohomology sheaves.
problems.check_method: Exact Chow-group example and actual cited primary reference
problems.decisive_evidence: H4_Zar(P²_Q,Z(2))=H²_Zar(P²_Q,K2)=CH²(P²_Q)=Z. A rational point has degree 1. Kahn printed p401 Theorem 1.6 explicitly includes 2<=i<=4 with H^{i-2}(K2); p411 projective-space computation gives Z term.
problems.result: The i=4 boundary in (2.22) is false and not supported by its cited theorem.
problems.counterevidence: Correct sheaf cohomology vanishes outside degrees 1,2; this can support a corrected fiber argument after a valid comparison map. Does not itself refute comparison theorem.
problems.impact: Incorrect intermediate vanishing used for the fiber argument following (2.22); minor local correction separate from Major P1.

correction.statement: Positive-degree global vanishing starts at i>4; use Kahn Remark 1.5 for sheaf-level fiber calculation.
correction.verification: Boundary and primary-reference statement verified; complete replacement proof not certified.
correction.author_adoption: Later author PDF p20 retains i>=4; no communication.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: The global vanishing assertion for H^i_Zar(-,Z(2)) in the paragraph following Theorem2.3.8, author-v2 p21, includes i=4. Its citation is checked against Kahn Theorem1.6, printed p401/PDF p7.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: For P?_Q, H4_Zar(P?,Z(2))=CH?(P?)=Z, witnessed by a degree-one point. Kahn's actual theorem includes the i=4 Chow group rather than its vanishing; the retained dependency's projective-space calculation at PDF p17 is consistent with this counterexample.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: The proof of Proposition2.3.11 needs the cohomology-sheaf range in degrees1 and2, which does not imply this false global-hypercohomology assertion. The fiber argument is not refuted by the example. The later author text also retains the erroneous global range.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: Correct the global statement to the actual theorem's range and distinguish sheaf cohomology from global hypercohomology in the fiber argument.

problems.title: Postnikov classification omits the component action
problems.claim: Maps_E1(H,B^{n+1}A) classifies all two-stage grouplike objects with identified pi0=H and pin=A.
problems.assumptions: Terminal site, n=1, H=C2, A=C3; convergent 1-truncated Postnikov tower.
problems.decisive_evidence: Objects h in C2, Aut(h)=C3, tensor a⊗b=a+(-1)^h b. Associativity yields a+(-1)^h b+(-1)^{h+k}c. Component action is inversion. Fibers of BC2 -> B³C3 have trivial action, hence the stated functor is not essentially surjective.
problems.result: False unrestricted classification and automatic-centrality remark; even H abelian counterexample applies at k=1.
problems.counterevidence: Forward map-to-extension construction remains valid; torus-connectedness and finite étale coefficients rule out this action in the geometric use. Later author pp12-13 omit old1.2.6-1.2.8.
problems.impact: Local preliminary generality error; no demonstrated failure of torus or main classification.

correction.statement: Require trivial H-action with identification data, or specify action rho and twisted Postnikov class.
correction.verification: Necessary condition and point-site obstruction verified. Arbitrary-site replacement coherence not independently proved.
correction.author_adoption: Passage absent in observed later author file; reason and author response not inferred.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: The claimed essential image in Section1.2.8, author-v2 p13, does not impose trivial pi0 action on the higher homotopy group.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: On the terminal site take pi0=C2 and automorphism group C3. The strict monoidal groupoid with objects h in C2 and tensor of automorphisms a tensor b=a+(-1)^h b is associative and has the nontrivial inversion action. A fiber of BC2 to B?C3 with the printed constant coefficients has trivial action and cannot recover it. This explicitly tests the omitted hypothesis in the stated unrestricted target.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: The forward fiber construction is not contradicted. Connected torus and finite ?tale coefficient hypotheses in the actual main use exclude this action obstruction. The later author text no longer contains the old paragraphs; no author motive or whole-version equivalence is inferred.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: Restrict the target to the trivial-action case or formulate the classification with the required twisted local coefficients.

problems.title: Global unit endomorphisms require connectedness
problems.claim: Natural E -> End(1) for global sections is an isomorphism without connectedness assumption on S.
problems.assumptions: S=Spec C disjoint union Spec C, G=G_m, A trivial, mu=0, E a permitted finite Q_l extension.
problems.decisive_evidence: Global category is product of its two untwisted component categories. End(1)=E×E, with diagonal E map; (1,0) not in image.
problems.result: False for the allowed disconnected base.
problems.counterevidence: Endomorphism sheaf is constant E; nonempty connected base gives global E. Section6.4 already assumes connectedness. Later author p64 explicitly corrects to sheaf and connectedness.
problems.impact: Local tensor-category claim, not a counterexample to connected-base field applications.

correction.statement: End sheaf(1)=E, global End(1)=H0(S,E); impose nonempty connected S for E.
correction.verification: Exact component computation; actual later author correction visually verified.
correction.author_adoption: Observed in separately retrieved later author PDF; no communication or priority claim.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Section6.1 on author-v2 p59 allows disconnected S but asserts the scalar field equals the global endomorphism ring of the tensor unit.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: Let S be two copies of Spec C, G=Gm, twisting datum zero and the permitted coefficient field E. Then End(1)=E?E, so the diagonal scalar map E to End(1) is not onto. The endomorphism sheaf is nevertheless the constant sheaf E; this separates the global and sheaf assertions.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: The connected-base statement used later in Section6.4 remains valid. The exact later-author p64 text explicitly uses the sheaf statement and connectedness, independently supporting this bounded repair without proving general version equivalence.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: Use the endomorphism sheaf statement, or impose connected S and identify global endomorphisms via H0.

clarifications.result: Strict Weyl relation is necessary beyond ordinary invariance with2-torsion; derived Hom retained in rank-one checks.
Finite-coefficient applicability not fully independently verified; no additional Proposition6.4.11 counterexample asserted.
